By establishing a clear physical descriptor, these findings introduce a novel strategy for designing next-generation thermal conductors.

Thermodynamic constraints further reveal universal bounds on spin–heat conversion and introduce a figure of merit for its efficiency, opening new perspectives for spin-controlled thermal radiation and photonic thermal devices.

summary: Aperiodic tilings lie between crystalline order and disorder, giving rise to unusual wave phenomena. Here, the authors investigate 2D wave transport in the recently discovered Hat monotile based on exciton-polariton lattices, revealing localized, critical, and extended states within its fractal spectrum. Simulations reveal anomalous wave spreading, ranging from superdiffusive to near-subdiffusive transport. The authors propose an optical pump-probe approach to explore these effects experimentally, opening new avenues for studying critical phenomena in reconfigurable polariton lattices.

title: Correlated insulating states in twisted double bilayer graphene on CrOCl enhanced by interfacial charge transfer effect
summary: Here, the authors investigate electrical transport in twisted double bilayer graphene (TDBG) on the antiferromagnetic material CrOCl (COC). At ultrahigh magnetic fields, an enhanced correlated insulating state is observed at half-filling of TDBG, which is attributed to the charge transfer effect between TDBG and COC. The authors further characterize the behavior of the correlated state by systematic temperature- and magnetic-field dependent measurements. Their results highlight the interfacial charge-related effect as a promising approach to manipulating the correlated states in moiré systems.
